request.spec:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now has a grace-days setting, and changing the sheet's today closes any open periods that are past their grace. All 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` pass under `bin/e2e`.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V40__sheet_grace_days.sql`, adds a `grace_days` column to the sheet. Blank (null) means off.
- **The setting:** `PUT /api/sheets/{id}/settings/grace-days` accepts a whole number of days or blank. It writes `SETTING_CHANGED ... key=grace-days value=<days>` (empty value when blank), and the settings response now includes the grace days. It isn't dated, so it takes effect from the next change of today. It works the same way as the existing period-numbering-from setting.
- **The auto-close:** after the new today is saved, `PeriodService.closePastGrace` closes every open period whose to-date plus the grace days is before the new today, earliest to-date first. It uses the same code path as a close by hand, so the totals are fixed the same way. Each close writes the usual `PERIOD_CLOSED` line with ` auto=yes` added at the end. The rollup lines are written after these, as the request asks.
- **How it's wired:** changing today now publishes a `TodayChanged` event, and `PeriodService` listens for it. This runs in the same transaction and avoids a circular dependency, since `PeriodService` already depends on `SheetService`.
- **Front end:** the settings form has a `setting-grace-days` input and a `setting-grace-days-current` display. A value that isn't a whole number shows the usual settings error.

**Decisions for you to confirm:**
- **No permission check on auto-close.** A close by hand requires the user's role to be allowed to close. The automatic close doesn't check this, so whoever changes today triggers the close even if they couldn't close a period by hand. Viewers still can't change today. I read "exactly as a close by hand would" as being about the effect, not the permission. If you want the check applied, it's a small change.
- **Changing today now locks the sheet** for the length of that transaction, the same way other sheet-wide changes do. This stops two users who change today at the same moment from closing the same periods twice.
